title: Keep the correction
hook: Comparing your attempt with the target shows which item you got wrong.

knows: reading short labels and comparing simple counts
doesNotKnow: Use feedback to locate a specific mismatch instead of only counting attempts.

objective: Use feedback to locate a specific mismatch instead of only counting attempts.

claims.text: Scenario, hook and prediction: Comparing your attempt with the target shows which item you got wrong. Which feedback locates the mistake? Correct option: Target beside attempt. All fixture labels, example words, dates, task durations and file fields are stipulated exercise data.
claims.source: Explicit exercise fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts and pure rules in studyModels.ts. All times, sizes, deadlines and outcomes describe this exercise only; no empirical productivity or learning effect is inferred. W-367 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): The old "useful evidence only if you compare it" overstated the case against Roediger & Karpicke 2006 (retrieval itself helps). New hook states only what the stage shows; hook in studyCatalog.ts and meta.json changed. Fixed after FC LH-1 dispute; awaiting fact-checker re-check. FC LH-4 (2026-10-14, fact-checker, W-380): verified: after Check the stage reveals the target row and marks each attempt position good/bad (reconstructionMatches), so the comparison shows which item is wrong; an attempt count would not. Statement is limited to what the stage shows. Record: company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH4-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Comparison marks each position, including errors. A count of attempts alone would not reveal which item needs correction.
claims.source: Roediger & Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning, Psychological Science 17(3),249–255, DOI10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x; publisher abstract retrieved 2026-10-13: https://www.psychologicalscience.org/journals/psychological-science/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x/ . Prose-passage experiments found delayed retention advantages for retrieval over restudy. This short exercise does not establish that effect for the learner. Fixture mappings and rules are explicit conventions, not empirical demonstrations. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Every displayed result is computed from the visible exercise state: recall. One short reconstruction; not a retention experiment. The reveal reports this same state and never translates its score into a personal productivity or memory benefit.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/studyModels.ts and src/components/lifehacks/StudyLesson.tsx, keep-the-error-feedback fixture in src/lib/lifehacks/studyCatalog.ts. Stage rules: check reconstructed token positions against the covered target; count exact matches out of three. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Side-by-side comparison locates the wrong position; a count or a bare 'wrong' does not say which item.
claims.source: Recall item for this lesson: stipulated example data and the rule taught in the lesson (company/reviews/lifehacks-200/recall-patch-study.md + recall-patch-study.lines.txt). Applies to the example only; no empirical effect is claimed. Recall patch by learning-designer (session 2, 2026-10-14), applied by session 1. Pointer corrected by demo-builder 2026-10-14 (W-391a). | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Convention and logic: an attempt count or a bare "wrong" carries no position information, while a side-by-side comparison marks each position; the stage does exactly this (reconstructionMatches gives a per-position true/false and each attempt box turns green or red after Check). The keyed option (index 1) is the only one that locates the error. No empirical learning claim is made.

recall.question: You wrote a five-step sequence from memory. Which feedback tells you what to fix?
options: A note saying this was your third attempt
Your attempt beside the target, errors marked
A note saying 'not quite, try again'
recall.why: Side-by-side comparison locates the wrong position; a count or a bare 'wrong' does not say which item.
